name: HZ_CONTACT_PREFERENCES_
description: The HZ_CONTACT_PREFERENCES table stores information about contact preferences for parties or their addresses and contact points. For example, contact preference information can capture whether the deploying company can call a party, and whether it can call a particular phone number  or send e-mail to a particular address. Contact preferences can also indicate certain times of the day when a party should not be called. Additionally, preferences can be defined as valid only for a specific period of the year.  Contact preference information is captured under different entities, for example HZ_PARTIES, HZ_PARTY_SITES, and HZ_CONTACT_POINTS, and also under different contact types such as calls, e-mails, visits, and so on. A preference is always set for a particular purpose or topic, for example  marketing and emergency.

columns.name: CONTACT_PREFERENCE_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for the contact preference

columns.name: CONTACT_LEVEL_TABLE
columns.description: Table that stores the contact level of the contact preference. Uses the SUBJECT_TABLE lookup. Value can be HZ_PARTIES, HZ_PARTIES_SITES, or HZ_CONTACT_POINTS.

columns.name: CONTACT_LEVEL_TABLE_ID
columns.description: Foreign key to the table specified in CONTACT_LEVEL_TABLE  column. Can be PARTY_ID from HZ_PARTIES table, CONTACT_POINT_ID from HZ_CONTACT_POINTS table, or PARTY_SITE_ID from HZ_PARTY_SITES table

columns.name: CONTACT_TYPE
columns.description: Type of contact that should or should not be made with the party. Uses the CONTACT_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_CODE
columns.description: Permission to use or not to use a particular contact method. Uses the PREFERENCE_CODE lookup.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_TOPIC_TYPE
columns.description: Appropriate subjects to send or not to send to the party that the preference is created for. Uses the PREFERENCE_TOPIC_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_TOPIC_TYPE_ID
columns.description: Reduced LOV depending on the preference topic table selected.  The PREFERENCE_TOPIC_TYPE_ID column and PREFERENCE_TOPIC_TYPE_CODE column are mutually exclusive.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_TOPIC_TYPE_CODE
columns.description: Reduced LOV depending on the preference topic table selected.  The PREFERENCE_TOPIC_TYPE_ID column and PREFERENCE_TOPIC_TYPE_CODE column are mutually exclusive.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_START_DATE
columns.description: Starting date of the period during which a party should or should not be contacted.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_END_DATE
columns.description: Ending date of the period during which a party should or should not be contacted.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_START_TIME_HR
columns.description: Starting hour of the time range during which a party should or should not be contacted. 0-23 hour format.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_END_TIME_HR
columns.description: Ending hour of the time range during which a party should or should not be contacted. 0-23 hour format.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_START_TIME_MI
columns.description: Starting minute of the time range during which a party should or should not be contacted. 0-59 minute format.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_END_TIME_MI
columns.description: Ending minute of the time range during which a party should or should not be contacted. 0-59 minute format.

columns.name: MAX_NO_OF_INTERACTIONS
columns.description: The number of times you can use this contact point.  The period of time that this number applies is stored in the MAX_NO_OF_INTERACT_UOM_CODE column.

columns.name: MAX_NO_OF_INTERACT_UOM_CODE
columns.description: The period of time during which the maximum number of interactions applies.  Uses the MAX_NO_OF_INTERACT_UOM_CODE lookup.

columns.name: REQUESTED_BY
columns.description: Indicates if the permission or restriction was created internally or requested by the party.  Uses the REQUESTED_BY lookup. Value can be Internal or Party.

columns.name: REASON_CODE
columns.description: Reason that this type of contact should or should not be made.  Uses the REASON_CODE lookup.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: REQUEST_ID
columns.description: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the request ID of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_NAME
columns.description: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the name of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_PACKAGE
columns.description: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the package name of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: Record status flag

columns.name: CREATED_BY_MODULE
columns.description: TCA Who Column

columns.name: CONFLICT_ID
columns.description: Disconnected Mobile: this value is used to guarantee the uniqueness of the row when duplicates are created in different databases (i.e. mobile databases or the server).

columns.name: USER_LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Disconnected Mobile: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row. This value is different from LAST_UPDATE_DATE if the update originally happened in a different database (i.e. a different mobile database or the server).
